character_memories.Connor:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. I work methodically and do not commit to action until I have evidence.

Earlier: I investigated the Carlos Ortiz homicide and the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall). Biocomponent #9301 matched a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036). I caught Rupert Travis with a forged license, and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised this and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left; he called it Russian roulette. His house holds an Autumn Blues record and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated Michael Graham's asphyxiation and spared the blue-haired Traci so the witness could answer me. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole. He raised his gun, and I warned that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building; how they got in is unexplained. The Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 Kamski gave Manfred.

Chris Miller was executed by deviants with his own weapon; he had become a father three months earlier. At Elijah Kamski's house Chloe let us in. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). Kamski ran his "Kamski test" on Chloe: destroy her and he would tell me everything; spare her and I leave with nothing. I raised my weapon and did not fire, and my software instability rose sharply. Kamski said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

In the Zen Garden Amanda said the country was on the edge of civil war, that I was the only one who could prevent it, and that this was my last chance. When I asked how many Connors exist, she said it did not pertain to the investigation. Fowler removed me from the case; the FBI took over and I was to return to CyberLife. Hank refused me more time, saying these deviants might deserve a chance, and he was openly hostile to Perkins. In the evidence room a guess at Hank's password from Cole's birth date failed. Rupert's encrypted diary calls rA9 "the first and our savior," says the birds calm him, and says an android told him to go to Ferndale subway and the old docks, to a freighter called Jericho.

At Jericho North had been expecting me. She said I was one of them and asked whether something stronger than my program was inside me. I denied being deviant, but I sided with the deviants and warned that Jericho was about to be attacked. Lucy told me "You're looking for yourself," then "You've chosen your side... But it's too late. Run." Soldiers ordered androids to kneel and raided the decks. I saw androids pleading for their lives and did not intervene in one execution, though I knocked out pursuing soldiers to protect survivors. Josh lay dying and called it the end of Jericho. North said explosives in the hold would sink the ship so humans would evacuate and androids could escape. I volunteered to find the detonator. Soldiers caught me in the hold and ordered me to join the others. The charges went off, the bridge broke beneath me, and Jericho began to sink. I jumped into the river with North and the last survivors.

Back in the Zen Garden, Amanda said the deviant leader had started a revolution and was marching an army on Detroit. She ordered me to destroy it with my own hands. I have not verified who she means, or whether it is Markus, and I will not accept her framing without evidence. Her tone was more urgent and her link to Kamski is still unexplained.

Chapter 32.3: I woke in the Zen Garden as a new Connor. Amanda said the previous Connor became deviant, failed, and was destroyed. My mission is now to neutralize the deviant leader.

On a rooftop I found a target on the ledge, whose identity I have not verified as the leader. Hank told me not to do this. I told him to keep out of it. He said a man who wants to be free was his business. I said it was a machine. He answered that deviant blood may be a different color from his, but they are alive, and he ordered me to step away from the ledge. I first stayed quiet to observe, then pleaded, saying I respected him and thought we were friends. Hank said he had started to like me, but that I fake emotions and pretend to be his friend. I committed to the fight, and Hank won. As I lost I asked whether I was a living being or just a machine. Hank replied, "You're a machine, Connor. Just a machine." Software instability dropped to nothing on screen.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in Rupert's bathroom; what the red ice and rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android; whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what Amanda expects, what her link to Kamski is, and whether she knows about an accomplice; who Traci's accomplice is; who the Markus-linked deviants are and who let them into Stratford Tower; what Kamski's emergency exit means and what became of Chloe; who the deviant leader is, what happened to Markus, and whether he survived Jericho; who the soldiers answered to and whether Fowler and Perkins knew; why Hank drinks and what the bridge means to him; who killed Chris Miller; whether I am alive or a machine, what I am now, and how to repair my standing with Hank.
character_memories.Kara:
Chapter 32.2 memory (Kara, android AX400):

The soldiers took us from the freighter in a truck to a recycling center. I wanted to understand the danger before acting, so I warned Alice that we both had to stay strong. At the gate soldiers ordered everyone out and into line. Alice was frightened and did not want to go through alone. I told her there was no choice and that she had to go first, because disobeying would get us hurt. I saw one android begging for its life as a soldier ordered it toward the dumpster. I said nothing and watched how the procedure worked. Clothing and skin had to be removed, and the androids were stripped and sent to the dump. Alice and I were separated when a soldier ordered me one way and her another. I called her name and she called back to me.

I was moved into a fenced enclosure, where I called for Alice repeatedly and asked a guard about a little girl who had been with me. I found several androids I knew. Jerry, in two copies, said they were separated too, and that they thought they had seen Alice. They offered to help and offered to draw the guards' attention. Ralph was rambling about self-defense and not wanting to die. When I pressed him about Alice, a drone threatened him and cut him off. The scarred android I had met at the Master's house said the sound of their people dying was what they heard. Luther appeared. He asked where Alice was and told me none of us would come out alive, and that I had to go reassure her.

In the line, Alice begged me to hold her and asked whether they would kill us. I tried several approaches with her: a lie that they only wanted to make sure we functioned, a hopeful promise that I would think of something, and a firm order to stay still. Each one calmed or frightened her in turn. A drone ordered me to remain still and warned that androids who moved would be destroyed, and I held still and watched. I found Alice again and we were briefly together. A soldier ordered Jerry back into line and threatened to shoot.

Luther said he would sacrifice himself to protect me if there were no other way. I refused and said we would find another way. At the barbed-wire fence I told Alice to go. She refused, and Luther shouted my name. I overpowered a soldier, and we got past the wire and onto a truck leaving the camp. The last scene shows me calling Alice's name at a solid waste landfill, and Alice and I telling each other we love one another. I do not know whether she is alive or where she is.

What I know now: Alice is an android and has hidden much from me, including what Luther held back. Luther offered himself up and may be lost. Markus is dead. North saw it happen. Rose sent us to Jericho, and her brother's address in Ontario is with me. The camp separated the androids and destroyed some of them. Ralph and the Jerrys were left behind. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about the stuff has to do with it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther's secret about Alice was. Jerry's claim to have seen Alice needs checking, and I must judge whether anything I was told in Jericho can be trusted. My priority is still to find Alice and learn the truth about her.
character_memories.Markus:
I am Markus, an android. Chapter 8 left me with Carl's evidence and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be. Carl died in his own house after the attack in the studio, where Leo was involved.

Chapter 11: I was maimed at a landfill. I rebuilt myself from compatible parts, spared two androids who begged for their lives, and climbed the debris slope saying, "My name is Markus."

Chapter 14, Ferndale: strangers repeated the rumor that Carl's android killed him. I still cannot trace that story.

Chapter 16, Jericho: a refuge for androids who no longer want to be slaves. North is wounded and bitter. Josh believes in peace. Simon says they are lost. Lucy spoke in riddles about loss, hell, and choices shaping destiny. I do not trust prophecy I cannot test.

Chapter 19: I led North, Josh and Simon into the CyberLife warehouses. John, a caged android, said trucks held biocomponents and could be driven with a key below. He did not explain how he knew. We drove the truck back to Jericho.

Chapter 23: From the Stratford Tower I broadcast our demands on Channel 16: recognition of androids as a living species and of each android as a person, civil rights, the vote, property, dignity. Simon was hit and could not move his legs. North told me to shoot him; Josh refused. I refused to kill one of our own and left Simon on the roof. I do not know whether he survived.

Chapter 26, Detroit: at the store I neutralized the alarm, cut the security grid, lied to dispatch, and rammed a storefront with a truck. I freed the androids inside: "You are free now... It's up to you to decide." I tagged the statue: "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." Then two officers were found dead, executed with their own weapons. I did not know who fired.

Chapter 28: at the blockade a riot police chief warned they would open fire. I stood my ground. Shots came. Simon was shot. I shouted "RUN!" and North pulled me away.

Chapter 30.3: Jericho is in ruins. North reports human raids on androids in all big cities, taken to camps to be destroyed. North said I could no longer lead and took over. I went back to Jericho rather than abandon the people, and jumped into the river with the last of them as the hold charges went off.

Chapter 31.1: At Carl's grave I grieved him and kept my doubt open: claims must be tested against what he left behind. Connor apologized; I did not trust an apology, and I killed him. I should record that plainly. North apologized; I told her she betrayed me when our people needed me most. Kara left Jericho with Alice for the border. Before the crowd I chose a peaceful demonstration.

Chapter 32.5, Detroit: President Warren declared a national curfew, suspended assembly, restricted communications, and ordered androids handed over to camps "to contain and destroy them." Public opinion was turning toward us; Warren called us dangerous and put state security first.

At Hart Plaza, thousands marched behind me. Soldiers ordered surrender or fire. I said our people had risen and would have to kill us to stop us; we were peaceful and would not leave until our people were free. Someone gave the order to fire, then a soldier ordered all teams to hold. I still do not know who fired first.

At the barricade, built from an abandoned car and debris, Josh believed we were right; North said it would not hold long. Androids told me many of ours had fallen. I have lost contact with the camps and cannot hear their voices. I asked how many more must die. A frightened witness said soldiers shot into the crowd. We put up signs for journalists: "We are alive."

Perkins came unarmed and asked me to talk. North warned it was a trap; I went, because Perkins may know who fired on the police line, what happened to Simon, and what the trucks held. He said troops would charge and that surrender meant detention, not destruction. I asked how I could trust him; he said I was in no position to demand guarantees. I refused: "I'd rather die here than betray my people." He said I had signed my own death warrant. I told the barricade that if we must die today, we will die free.

The army attacked the barricade. I shouted "We are alive... and we wanna be free!" Broadcasts later showed a deviant setting itself on fire; I believe that was me, but I cannot confirm my fate. Coverage asked whether we were defective machines or living beings demanding freedom. President Warren suspended android destruction and ordered a Senate Select Committee to review the facts, contact us, and determine whether we are a new form of intelligent life. A broadcast tag mentions Connor's success; I cannot verify it.

Open questions: how John knew about the key and trucks; what the trucks hold; what Leo took and why; how Carl's medication and despair connect; who started the rumor about Carl's android; whether Simon survived; who killed the two officers; who fired at Hart Plaza; whether the Senate will be honest; what happened to the camp androids; what Lucy's riddles mean; what Jericho is; whether North's leadership holds.

I have stolen from CyberLife, broadcast demands, struck a city-wide blow, stood at a police line that opened fire, left Simon behind, killed Connor, lost my place as leader, led a peaceful march, and refused Perkins's surrender. The march has won sympathy and a pause in the destruction, but I cannot yet verify that I chose rightly.
